text.p: Ship charter company Osprey Maritime Ltd said on Monday it saw reason for optimism over the prospects for its 1997 results.
Osprey Maritime said in a statement with its 1996 full-year results that the company had overcome some recent difficulties involving problems with one of its vessels.
"The fleet expansion in 1996 and the completion of a new building programme in 1997 give rise for optimism for the current financial year's prospects," the statement said.
Tim Cottew, Osprey's chairman, said in a separate statement:
"We are confident that with the recent structural reorganisation of Osprey we will be able to seize the opportunities in the oil and gas industry and continue to see strong growth."
Osprey earlier reported a three percent rise in 1996 net profit to US$16.01 million.
